acme_support: Hey team — customer reported a streaming response that abruptly ends. They get a bunch of tokens then connection closes, response is not valid JSON (trailing comma). finish_reason is missing. Repro steps attached.
maria_support: Thanks, can you paste the exact request headers and SDK/version? Also need request_id and region.
acme_support: Request id: req_0x9f8a, region: us-west-2, model: open-vicuna-13b, SDK: node 2.4.1. They use the streaming SSE endpoint via our hosted API. Example curl they used:
acme_support: ```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \\n  -d '{"model":"open-vicuna-13b","input":"summarize ...","stream":true}' \\n  https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/streams
```
devon_engineer: Do we see any server-side disconnects around req_0x9f8a? jason, can you check the egress/proxy logs for 2025-11-02T17:04 UTC (approx)?
jason_sre: Looking now. Proxy shows a 502 on the backend connection at 17:04:12 for that req_id. Upstream runtime reported a short TCP FIN while streaming tokens. I'm seeing a sequence: a few `data:` SSE events, then connection closed. No finish token emitted by the runtime.
maria_support: Any recent deploys to runtime around that time? ingest-bot, deploys?
ingest-bot: Canary runtime image v3.14 deployed to us-west-2 at 2025-11-02T16:58:05 UTC to 17:02:00 UTC window.
devon_engineer: Hmm, canary rolled during that window. Two hypotheses: 1) in-flight streamed responses didn't get the finish sentinel when the worker was drained; or 2) resume/fallback header mismatch left a partial KV cache and truncated emit. Need repro. Can you try forcing a client reconnect quickly to simulate? Also include `Resume-Token` header that clients use in reconnect flows.
acme_support: Customer says they do a quick reconnect when their mobile goes background/foreground. Their reconnect flow sets `Resume-Token: tkn_123`. They saw truncated output ~70% of the time when reconnect happens within 2s of original finish. They attached a small repro script.
maria_support: Can you share the repro script? If we can reproduce locally we can test fast reconnect + canary drain.
acme_support: ```
// minimal node repro
const res1 = await fetch(streamUrl, { headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer $T', 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }, method: 'POST', body: JSON.stringify({model:'open-vicuna-13b', input:'long output...', stream:true}) });
// read a few events, then abort and reopen with Resume-Token header
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 800);
// reopen with resume token
await fetch(streamUrl, { headers: {'Resume-Token':'tkn_123', Authorization:'Bearer $T', 'Accept':'text/event-stream'}, method:'POST', body: JSON.stringify({resume:true}) });
```
devon_engineer: Reproduced locally with canary build v3.14. When worker is drained mid-emit, the runtime emits partial SSE and the HTTP stream is closed by the orchestrator without sending the finish sentinel. The partial payload ends with `,...` (trailing comma) so JSON fails to parse client-side. finish_reason absent because runtime never called the finalizer.
jason_sre: Stack: orchestrator sent SIGTERM to worker, worker closed streams before flushing final SSE frame. We also see the resume token tombstone routine marking session as stale; on reconnect the resume path returns a shortened token stream fragment (no finisher). That explains the missing finish_reason on reconnect.
maria_support: Next steps: 1) collect full server logs for the req_id and the worker PID; 2) ask eng-runtime to ensure graceful flush on SIGTERM (attempt retry or flush final frame); 3) consider server-side keepalive to let client drain. Also request we add a transient validation on client side that treats trailing commas gracefully as a safety net.
devon_engineer: For immediate mitigation we can: a) make orchestrator send a 10s delay/proactive drain when a worker hosts active streaming sessions; b) have the runtime attempt to emit a `finish_reason: 'server_restart'` sentinel before exit if possible; c) make resume flow validate full JSON by concatenating fragments server-side before sending resume payloads.
acme_support: Customer asked for a workaround they can apply now. Any client-side suggestions we can give them?
maria_support: Ask them to delay reconnect by 500-1000ms after abort, or treat a sudden connection close as potentially complete and attempt a small backfill with the normal non-streaming /completion endpoint to fetch final result. Also suggest adding resilient JSON parsing (strip trailing commas) temporarily.
jason_sre: Filed incident ticket RINF-2379 and assigned to eng-runtime (devon_engineer). Added canary tag. Will follow up once we have a fix and patch release plan.
maria_support: Thanks everyone. acme_support, I'll reply to the customer with the workaround and ETA for the fix. Please attach their repro and the request id in the ticket. :thumbsup:
